note: Original performance-based questions written for Patch Notes, in the style of CompTIA's. They are not real exam questions.

pbqs.title: Match the service to its port
pbqs.scenario: You're writing firewall rules for a small office and need the default port for each service.
pbqs.prompt: Choose the default port for each service.

items.why: TCP 22. Telnet (23) does the same job without encryption.
TCP 25. Mail clients usually submit on 587 instead.
UDP 53 for most lookups, TCP 53 for large answers and zone transfers.
The server listens on UDP 67 and the client on 68.
UDP 161 for polling; traps arrive on 162.
TCP 3389. Exposed to the internet, it's a favourite way in for ransomware gangs.

pbqs.title: Fill in the subnet table
pbqs.scenario: A colleague has noted three addresses from the network. For each, work out its subnet's details.

pbqs.title: Fix the staff VLAN on S3
pbqs.scenario: After last night's change, PC4 (Staff, on S3) can't reach PC1 (Staff, on S2), though PC1 and the other staff PCs work. VLANs 10, 20, 30, 99 and 150 exist on every switch, and the S1 to S2 trunk is fine. Find and fix what's wrong on S3, prove it, and save your work.

tasks.why: It had been set to access mode, so only VLAN 1 crossed it. show interfaces trunk on S1 shows no trunk on Gi0/2 until it's fixed.

tasks.text: Both ends of the S1 to S3 trunk use native VLAN 99, like the rest of the network.
tasks.why: A new trunk starts with native VLAN 1. A mismatch leaks untagged traffic between VLANs, and CDP warns about it.

tasks.text: PC4's port (S3 Fa0/11) is an access port in VLAN 10, Staff.
tasks.why: It had been put in VLAN 20 (Students). show vlan brief on S3 lists Fa0/11 under the wrong VLAN.

tasks.text: From PC4, a ping to PC1 (10.10.10.11) succeeds.
tasks.why: Proving the fix: PC4 and PC1 are now in the same VLAN, joined by working trunks.

tasks.text: S3's configuration is saved, so the fix survives a reload.
tasks.why: copy running-config startup-config (or wr) after the last change. Unsaved changes are lost when a switch restarts.

pbqs.simplification: The same simulated Cisco 2960 switches (IOS 15) as the VLAN lab: only the commands it models work. On the exam a PBQ like this may show a diagram and ask you to choose settings rather than type.

pbqs.title: Follow the troubleshooting method
pbqs.scenario: A user can't open the file server. Put these actions in the order CompTIA's troubleshooting method uses.

steps.text: Ask the user what changed and when, and check whether others are affected
steps.why: Identify the problem: gather information and question users.

steps.text: Suspect last night's switch change put their port in the wrong VLAN
steps.why: Establish a theory of probable cause.

steps.text: Check the port with show vlan brief: it's in VLAN 20, not 10
steps.why: Test the theory to confirm the cause.

steps.text: Plan to move the port back during the next change window, and tell the team
steps.why: Establish a plan of action and identify its effects.

steps.text: Have the user open the file server, and add the port to the change checklist
steps.why: Verify full functionality and put preventive measures in place.

steps.text: Write the cause and the fix in the ticket

pbqs.title: Match the symptom to the fault
pbqs.scenario: Tickets from a busy morning on a small office network. Each symptom points to one likely cause.
pbqs.prompt: Choose the most likely cause for each symptom.
choices: Mismatched fibre optics (SR at one end, LR at the other)

items.text: A laptop shows 169.254.40.12 and can't reach anything
items.why: 169.254.x.x is APIPA: the laptop asked for an address and got no answer.

items.text: A server link is slow and the switch counts late collisions on that port
items.why: One end at full duplex and the other at half gives late collisions and poor throughput. Set both ends the same (or both to auto).

items.text: CRC errors keep climbing on one access port; the cable runs past a lift motor
items.why: Corrupted frames fail their checksum. A bad termination or interference from heavy electrical equipment are classic causes.

items.text: A new fibre uplink never comes up, though both ends are 10 Gbit/s optics
items.answer: Mismatched fibre optics (SR at one end, LR at the other)
items.why: Short-reach and long-reach optics use different wavelengths and fibre types, so the link stays down.

items.text: A PC can ping everything on its own subnet but nothing beyond it
items.why: Local traffic doesn't need the gateway; anything off-subnet does.

items.text: Two PCs keep warning about an address conflict and drop off in turn
items.why: Two devices claiming one address take turns being reachable. Usually a static address inside the DHCP scope.

items.text: Users can reach 192.0.2.10 by address but not intranet.example by name
items.why: Working by IP but not by name points at name resolution.

items.text: After a desk move, one PC gets an address from the guest range
items.why: The address range comes from the VLAN's DHCP scope, so the new port is in the guest VLAN.
